functions.defect: The RESPONDED branch ends with `return query` and no `return;`. PL/pgSQL appends rows and CONTINUES, so both the idempotent-retry and conflicting-outcome paths fall through into the UPDATE and the audit INSERT. A conflicting second outcome overwrites the first while the caller — which reads only data[0] — is told 'already_responded'; a retry rewrites responded_at and appends a duplicate audit row while the caller is told 'unchanged'; every such call returns two rows.
functions.decisionReason: Repository authority and live carry the IDENTICAL defect and fail the identical six cases, so neither can be canonical. Choosing live merely to avoid changing production would preserve a body that silently overwrites a learner's first recorded outcome and corrupts an append-only audit.
